title: First even-moment benchmark
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and let $\mu$ be a probability distribution on $\Omega$. Suppose $r$ is a positive integer and the expectation of $X^2$ under $\mu$ is $1$. Then the expectation of $X^2$ cannot exceed the first even-moment benchmark $(2r-1)r/\binom{2r}{2}$.
